scenes.line1: Why do big queries run so fast?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how massive datasets can be queried in seconds? What's the secret behind blazing-fast analytics?

scenes.label: Pruning
scenes.sub: Warehouses skip irrelevant partitions for speed.
scenes.say: Partition pruning means your data warehouse only scans partitions that match your query filter. This speeds up queries by skipping unnecessary data.
If your sales table is partitioned by sale date, this query scans only the partition for June first, not the whole table.

scenes.label: Clustering
scenes.sub: Organizes rows inside partitions for fast filtering.
scenes.say: Clustering arranges data within partitions by columns you filter or join on. Related rows are grouped, so scans are even faster.

scenes.question: How do you pick partition keys?
scenes.right: Pick columns used in frequent query filters to maximize pruning and speed.
scenes.say: Interviewers love asking about partition key design. Don't say you pick random columns; always base your choice on common query filters to maximize performance.
